findings.quote: In connection with the Plan, the Company plans to reduce its workforce by up to 70%, with the majority of the reduction expected to be completed by the end of June 2022.

findings.finding: Five directors resigned on June 16, 2022, citing efforts to align resources and not any disagreement; another director resigned in October 2022, and new directors were added in January and August 2023.
findings.numbers: five director resignations; board reduced to five members
findings.quote: Following their decisions to resign from the Board, the Board reduced its size to five members, effective immediately.

charts: Revenue and net income over time

assessment.answer: The score of 0.582 comes from a tiny balance sheet ($10.5M of assets) carrying $47.9M of liabilities (4.57x assets against a peer median of 0.45), a current ratio of 0.09 against a peer median of 3.51, almost no revenue, and an annualized net loss about four times total assets. The filings show this is real distress and not an artefact. Cash was $1.8M at June 30 and $0.8M by August 9, 2023, against $16.5M of accounts payable and a burn of about $1.5M a month. That leaves roughly one month of cash, or less, and management itself says it would likely have to file for bankruptcy protection without adequate financing.
moved_by: Cash of $0.8M on August 9, 2023 against $16.5M of accounts payable; at the Q2 burn of about $4.6M per quarter (~$1.5M/month) that is about half a month of cash, or about 1.2 months from the $1.8M June 30 balance
Management explicitly states it would likely have to file for bankruptcy protection and wind down if it cannot obtain adequate financing, and says its plans cannot be assessed as probable

History of nonpayment to suppliers, including the primary contract manufacturer, which led to a forbearance agreement with acceleration rights if any payment is more than 60 days late; payments start October 2023 with almost no cash to make them
$15.0M convertible note with events of default including bankruptcy events and judgments of $3.0M or more, adding to liabilities
Landlord lawsuit over the abandoned Stow lease and Healios's allegation of material breach of the Framework Agreement
Nasdaq Panel exception only through September 15, 2023 on the $35M market value standard plus a new $1.00 bid price deficiency, which threaten access to equity capital
New financing is very small (about $3.4M net in April 2023), and the Aspire $100M equity facility was terminated in July 2022
NT 10-Q late filing for the June 2023 quarter

reasons.reason: Liabilities far exceed assets; stockholders' deficit widened to $37.4M
reasons.numbers: total liabilities $47.9M vs total assets $10.5M (4.57x); stockholders' deficit $(37,419) thousand at June 30, 2023 vs $(23,851) thousand at December 31, 2022
reasons.peer_comparison: liabilities/assets 4.57 vs peer median 0.45; total liabilities at 95th peer percentile as a share of assets

reasons.reason: Current liabilities are about 11 times current assets; the company cannot cover near-term obligations
reasons.numbers: current assets $3.7M vs current liabilities $42.7M; current ratio 0.09; current assets fell from $21.4M a year earlier
reasons.peer_comparison: current ratio 0.09 vs peer median 3.51; current liabilities at 95th percentile, current assets at 19th percentile

reasons.reason: Large losses relative to the asset base
reasons.numbers: annualized net income -$41.5M (-395.8% of assets); operating income -$40.6M; Q2 net loss $(12,924) thousand
reasons.peer_comparison: net income and operating income at 5th peer percentile

reasons.reason: Cash runway is about one month or less. Q2 burn = $10.6M (6M) minus $6.0M (Q1) = $4.6M, about $1.5M/month; $1.8M at June 30 is about 1.2 months, and $0.8M at August 9 is about half a month. Over six months the burn averaged about $1.8M/month
reasons.numbers: cash $1.8M (June 30, 2023), $0.8M (August 9, 2023); operating cash used $10.6M for 6M 2023, $6.0M for Q1 2023; accounts payable $16.5M
reasons.peer_comparison: operating cash flow at 8th peer percentile
reasons.quote: As of August 9, 2023, we had $0.8 million of cash and cash equivalents and accounts payable of $16.5 million, of which $8.7 million is related to deferred accounts payable to supplier.

reasons.reason: Management explicitly names bankruptcy as the likely outcome if financing is not obtained
reasons.quote: If we are unable to obtain adequate financing, we likely would have to file for protection under the bankruptcy laws to continue to pursue potential transactions and conduct a wind down of our Company.
reasons.source: 10-Q, 2023-08-16, Note 2. Going Concern; MD&A Liquidity and Capital Resources

reasons.reason: Going concern doubt, with management saying its plans cannot be assessed as probable
reasons.quote: these plans are not entirely within our control and cannot be assessed as being probable of occurring.

reasons.reason: The forbearance agreement followed overdue supplier payments, and the supplier can accelerate if any payment is more than 60 days late; payments begin October 2023
reasons.numbers: $11.8M deferred payables at $0.25M monthly from October 2023; 60-day acceleration trigger
reasons.quote: If any cash payment remains unpaid for more than 60 days following the date such cash payment was due, the supplier has the right to declare the entire remaining balance due immediately and payable without further notice.
reasons.source: 10-Q, 2023-08-16, Note 11. Forbearance Agreement and Convertible Note

reasons.reason: A new $15.0M PIK convertible note adds debt with default triggers, including judgments of $3.0M or more
reasons.numbers: principal $15.0M; 10% PIK (14% on default); maturity May 17, 2026; fair value $15.8M
reasons.quote: certain events of bankruptcy and an adverse judgment for payment of $3.0 million or more (each, an “Event of Default”).

reasons.reason: Nonpayment to the contract manufacturer is delaying clinical supply, which threatens the MASTERS-2 trial that future financing depends on
reasons.quote: continued delays in product supply caused by nonpayment to our primary contract manufacturer for our clinical trials may impact the timing and cost of such studies.

reasons.numbers: Q2 2023 revenue $48.8 thousand vs $2.3M; annualized revenue $0.1M vs $10.5M a year earlier
reasons.quote: Revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2023 were $48.8 thousand compared to $2.3 million for the three months ended June 30, 2022.

reasons.reason: Nasdaq listing is at near-term risk, which would further limit equity raising
reasons.numbers: $35M market value standard, Panel deadline September 15, 2023; $1.00 bid price, deadline January 24, 2024
reasons.quote: the Panel notified us that it had granted our request for an exception through September 15, 2023, to the continued listing requirements, subject to our demonstrating compliance with the Market Value Standard by September 15, 2023.

reasons.reason: Litigation and disputes: the landlord sued over the Stow lease, and Healios alleges material breach
reasons.numbers: landlord claim in excess of $25,000, amount undetermined
reasons.quote: Healios has alleged that we are in material breach of our Framework Agreement for, among other things, not meeting our supply obligations and cooperation and assistance obligations.

reasons.reason: Executives are deferring pay to preserve cash, and the company filed late for the quarter
reasons.quote: To preserve liquidity in the Company, named executive officers, including severance to former executives, have agreed to defer compensation.

evidence_against.point: The supplier restructuring pushed most overdue cash payments out to October 2023 and later, and produced a gain on extinguishment, easing immediate pressure
evidence_against.quote: The Company recorded a gain on extinguishment of $2.6 million as a result of the restructuring.

evidence_against.point: Cash burn has fallen sharply after the 70% workforce cut (6M operating cash used $10.6M vs $36.6M a year earlier)
evidence_against.quote: Net cash used in operating activities was $10.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2023 compared to $36.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2022.

evidence_against.point: Part of the period's loss is non-cash (a $7.5M right-of-use impairment plus fair value changes), so the annualized net loss overstates cash losses
evidence_against.quote: the Company recorded an impairment charge related to the right-of-use asset of $7.5 million.

evidence_against.point: The company can still raise small amounts of equity (April 2023, about $3.4M net)
evidence_against.quote: The offering closed on April 19, 2023, and the Company received net proceeds of approximately $3.4 million, after giving effect to the payment of placement fees and expenses.

evidence_against.point: The August 2023 MOU with Healios brings a small deposit and possible further compensation, and suggests the relationship may be stabilizing
evidence_against.quote: Pursuant to the MOU, Healios has deposited $150,000 with the Company to be applied to the charges incurred for these consultation services.

evidence_against.point: The $15.0M note is PIK and does not mature until May 2026, so it needs no near-term cash
evidence_against.quote: The Note bears interest at a rate of 10.0% per annum, which shall be capitalized and added to the principal amount semi-annually on January 1 and July 1, commencing on July 1, 2023

Any new financing announcement in the next 1-2 months, since cash on August 9 covered only about two weeks to a month of burn
Outcome of the Stow landlord lawsuit and the Healios breach dispute (a judgment of $3.0M or more is an event of default under the note)

MASTERS-2 trial progress and clinical product supply

A sale of the company or its assets outside court
Proof that the forbearance payments from October 2023 are being made and that the Nasdaq listing is maintained
Positive MASTERS-2 data that opens access to capital

Whether the Nasdaq Panel deadline of September 15, 2023 will be met
The amount the Stow landlord is seeking beyond 'in excess of $25,000'
Whether Healios will start formal legal proceedings over the alleged breach
